# EquinoxNG: Next Generation E-Graph Library and RDVSG Rewriter

EqunoxNG is the header-only version of my own e-graph library, [Equinox](https://github.com/Chubek/Equinox). Keep in mind that, both Equinox and EquinoxNG are 'AI Slop'. But let me tell you a story.

My dad was a pediatric dentist, and his friend's father, who ended up becoming his brother-in-law, whose generous donations has funded all these "AI Slop", taught pathology at that university. And, between me and you, he despised my father, and he and I are the only people on earth who truly knew that my father was a piece of absolute garbage.

Anyways, at the time, new devices had arrived that could diagnose a patients markers just with a drop of blood. Much larger amount of blood than that lady who went to jail promised, but still.

He believed pathologists who rely on these machines are not 'real' pathologists. But had he reflected, he'd realized, the chemicals the previous generated had used, had replaced doctors in the Vicotiran era tasting stool samples to find out what is wrong.

Now you understand why reliance on AI agents to write code is going to replace manual coding?

Let me refer to you Peter Naur's 1985 paper, [Programming as Theory Building](https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/Naur.pdf). In this papser, Naur argues that programming is not mainly about drinking coffee and churning shitcode, as people who call themselves "Devs" and have to rely on frameworks size of an operating system to write a landing page for a some company that is basicaly a pyramid scheme. He argues that it is about "understanding of a system". The real program is not source code. AI coding gets rid of the painful stage between *realizing a system* and *understanding a system*.

So, yeah. There were no true e-graph libraries for C++, now there's an e-graph + RDVSG framework, plus a language that rewrites expressions, called EQVSG. 

Read the documentation.
